name: South London Gallery
known: Wikipedia says the London Borough of Southwark took over responsibility for the gallery in 1965 under independent trustees, that David Thorp was appointed director in 1992 and that Margot Heller became director in 2001.

The trustees, chaired by Matthew Slotover, voted by majority in 2018 to return the grant after it had been banked, because of potential reputational damage; the article notes that much of the Sackler money comes from OxyContin proceeds, and other donors then funded the education centre (The Art News

name: Studio Voltaire
known: Joe Scotland is director (Wikipedia).
The Studio Voltaire Council core funds the programmes; its co-chairs are Ruth Chapman, Thomas Dane and Jill Garcia.
Studio Voltaire co-founded Common Practice, belongs to Allied Editions and CVAN London, and delivers the Syllabus programme with Wysing Arts Centre, Eastside Projects, Spike Island and Iniva.

name: Whitechapel Gallery
known: Charles Aitken was the first director, 1901 to 1911 (Wikipedia).
The 2021-22 annual report showed a deficit of £73,016; the gallery restructured in 2023 and made six full-time staff redundant, three of them curators (USA Art News, 16 March 2023).
Whitechapel Gallery runs the Max Mara Art Prize for Women with Collezione Maramotti, the NEON Curatorial Award with NEON in Athens, and belongs to Allied Editions.

name: Zabludowicz Collection
known: Poju Zabludowicz is founder and trustee (Wikipedia).
Boycotted since 2014 over the founder's ties.

name: HOME
known: Dave Moutrey, long-time chief executive and artistic director, has left.
HOME is led by joint chief executives Karen O'Neill and Sita McIntosh (The Mill, 7 April 2024).

name: The Whitworth
known: Sook-Kyung Lee has been director since August 2023.
Alistair Hudson, director from 2018, announced in July 2022 that he would leave at the end of 2022 for ZKM Karlsruhe (Museums Journal, 22 July 2022).

name: The Crab Museum
known: Founded by Chase Coley and brothers Bertie and Ned Suesat-Williams, none with a crab or museum background (Wikipedia).
The three are the directors of Crab Museum CIC, incorporated on 26 September 2019 (Companies House).
The directors are Chase John Coley, Rachada Edmund Suesat-Williams and Satakalet Bertie Suesat-Williams, all appointed on 26 September 2019.
Start-up money came from the three directors' savings, now depleted; each spent a year earning money to put in (Museums Association, 2023).

name: MIMA
known: Its first director, Godfrey Worsdale, left in 2008 for the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art (Wikipedia).
The building holds gallery spaces, an education suite, an auditorium, a cafe-bar, a shop, a roof terrace, collection stores and a conservation studio.
MIMA works closely with Teesside University staff, and its Director is also the university's Dean of Culture & Creativity.

name: MK Gallery
known: Director is Anthony Spira.

name: New Art Exchange
known: Formed in 2003 by the merger of two grassroots groups: APNA Arts, a South Asian arts collective founded by Parbinder Singh, and East Midlands African Caribbean Arts, co-founded with educationalist and historian Len Garrison (Wikipedia).
Saad Eddine Said was appointed Chief Executive Officer and Artistic Director in 2021.
Unrestricted reserves stood at 3,914,436 pounds; the chair of trustees is Samori Gambrah and the vice chair Professor Christopher O'Brien (accounts).
New Art Exchange was formed in 2003 as a partnership between APNA Arts and EMACA Visual Arts, and it co-chairs CVAN England.
